reason: This text (Genesis 2:8–3:24) does not support the statement for multiple reasons: (1) It is fundamentally anachronistic—the passage describes primordial human creation, not the Hebrew people as a distinct group, which emerged millennia later; (2) Yahweh's actions toward humanity are consistently benevolent: He plants a garden, causes pleasant and nourishing trees to grow, creates a companion because solitude is 'not good,' and provides abundantly. (3) The prohibitions (not eating from one tree) and subsequent consequences are presented as boundary-setting and enforcement of divine law, not antagonism. (4) Antagonism implies hostility or opposition; the text instead shows God establishing order and natural consequences for transgression. (5) The Jewish interpretive tradition consistently understands this passage as establishing God's sovereignty and humanity's free will, not divine hostility.
